thread:
incident-bot: ALERT: High CPU usage in preproc/tokenize service in eu-west-1 cluster — 80% pod OOMs. Pager engaged for oncall(s): @sophie. Priority: P1 :rotating_light:

sophie (oncall): Seeing lots of pod restarts on tokenizer-preproc-*.cpu pods. Metrics show CPU usage spiking to 400% on some nodes, kernel OOM events. Paging now.

raj (sre): Got the page, joining. Can you paste the cluster + node list and any recent deploys?

sophie (oncall): No deploys in the last hour according to deploy-bot. kubectl get pods -n inference | grep preproc shows ~15 CrashLoopBackOff across 3 nodes.

sophie (oncall): quick logs from one pod:
```
E0423 14:02:11.123456 1 tokenizer.cpp:234 DynamicTokenizer::process() CPU spike detected, spinning in regex loop
terminate called after throwing an instance of 'std::bad_alloc'
Aborted (core dumped)
```

jun (eng-ml): That regex backtrack pattern has bitten us before for very long prompts. We're seeing very large user prompts in the last 15m (ingest rates x6).

maria (customer-success): Notifying top 3 customers on the next update. Any ETA for mitigation? Some are in mid-day for EU.

tim (eng-runtime): Looking at node logs — I see oom_killer invoked for pid 4213 on node eu-west1-n3. Also kubelet reporting container killed for memory. We might be getting queue starvation; preproc pods hog CPU doing weird backtracking which causes kernel to OOM.

raj (sre): Immediate mitigation options: 1) scale down tokenizer replica weight for non-critical tenants, 2) cordon/evict offending pods to flatten load, 3) roll a config to apply a hard CPU limit to preproc container to prevent runaway. Which do we want first?

sophie (oncall): Start with cordon + evict on the three nodes with most OOMs (eu-west1-n3,n4,n6) so we stop cascading. I'll trigger a taint to prevent new preproc pods scheduling while we stabilize.

raj (sre): executing: `kubectl taint nodes eu-west1-n3 node-role.kubernetes.io/isolated=true:NoSchedule --overwrite` and cordon on n4/n6.

[deploy-bot]: Rollout history: no recent tokenizer-preproc changes. Last config change 6d ago.

sophie (oncall): Evicting pods now from n3/n4/n6 (grace 30s) and forcing scheduler to spread to less loaded nodes.

tim (eng-runtime): Heads up: while restarting a few pods on a recovered node, I see GPU driver warn: "CUDA driver lost: incompatible ELF header" on node eu-west1-n2 when a restart touched accelerator-attached nodes. Not sure if related but noted.

jun (eng-ml): That CUDA error is suspect — maybe a mismatch after a node upgrade earlier? But preproc is CPU-bound, shouldn't touch GPUs. Could be a side effect of other services restarting.

sophie (oncall): Customer impact: A subset of inference requests in eu-west-1 failing with 502s and long tail latency. Maria, please flag high-usage customers and prepare template for status.

maria (customer-success): On it. Drafting: "We are mitigating a tokenizer pre-processing CPU surge causing retries and 502s for some requests in EU. Engineers are taking steps to isolate and restart affected pods. We'll update in 15m."

raj (sre): Next mitigation: push a config tweak to tokenizer-preproc to enable a lightweight fallback tokenizer for very long prompts and set request-size cap at the ingress layer. I can prepare a safe patch and canary to 10% traffic.

tim (eng-runtime): I support that. Also recommend adding a liveness probe tweak to avoid rapid restarts (increase initialDelaySeconds) so pods don't thrash the node and cause OOM storms.

sophie (oncall): Agree. Can we do the safe hotfix now? I can take the canary and watch.

raj (sre): Creating 2-step hotfix: 1) apply CPU limit 1.5 core and memory 1Gi to tokenizer-preproc container, 2) swap tokenizer binary to "fast-fallback" build that avoids pathological regex. Patch manifest attached.

raj (sre): Applying patch to deployment tokenizer-preproc -> `kubectl apply -f preproc-hotfix-2245.yaml` (canary selector label preproc-canary: true).

[deploy-bot]: Started rollout preproc-hotfix-2245 -> tokenizer-preproc (canary 10%) by raj.

sophie (oncall): Canary pods up. Observing CPU on canary ~60% and no backtrack logs. Good sign. No OOMs on nodes hosting canary.

jun (eng-ml): Confirmed fallback tokenizer reduces tokenization time on long prompts by ~7x in our local benchmark.

tim (eng-runtime): After canary stable for 6 minutes, I recommend increment to 40% then 100% if stable. Also we should drain the worst nodes after patch so they don't keep flapping.

sophie (oncall): Proceeding to 40%.

[~5 minutes pass]

sophie (oncall): 40% looks stable. Rolling to 100% now. Monitoring for memory pressure.

[deploy-bot]: Rollout complete: preproc-hotfix-2245 -> tokenizer-preproc (100%) by raj.

tim (eng-runtime): Post-rollout: CPU utilization across preproc fleet down to normal baseline, OOM events stop. However, eu-west1-n2 still shows intermittent "CUDA: ioctl error" logs from unrelated gpu-attach service — opened infra ticket INFRA-2245.

maria (customer-success): Customer update sent. Several customers replied asking for root cause. They're happy to hear rollback mitigation worked.

sophie (oncall): Oncall notes: - Mitigation: applied fallback tokenizer + CPU caps + liveness probe tuning. - Actions: cordon + drain three nodes, escalate CUDA driver mismatch to infra, follow-up postmortem scheduled.

raj (sre): I'll start the post-incident timeline and collect logs, flamegraphs, and the payloads causing regex backtrack. Need any specific handoffs?

jun (eng-ml): Will take lead on creating a deterministic test to reproduce pathological prompts and add fuzzing to early validation.

tim (eng-runtime): I'll handle the infra ticket for the GPU driver error. Could be a separate rolling update gone wrong.

maria (customer-success): I'll follow up with impacted customers with cause and mitigation summary once postmortem is ready.

sophie (oncall): Handoff: I'm going offline in 25m; raj will be oncall until EOD. Leaving Slack handover: look for lingering OOM events and any new 502s.

raj (sre): Acknowledged, taking over. Will keep this thread updated. :white_check_mark:

incident-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: mitigated — services stable in eu-west-1. Postmortem scheduled in #postmortems for 2024-04-24 10:00 UTC.

sophie (oncall): thanks all — great triage.

raj (sre): logging timeline and tagging artifacts: logs: `s3://redwood-incidents/2245123456/*`, flamegraphs: `s3://redwood-incidents/2245123456/flamegraphs/`, payload sample set in secure bucket.
